claims.text: Under dynamic loading, CrMnFeCoNi near its deformation-induced transformation limit generates localized deformation twins.
Under dynamic loading, CrMnFeCoNi near its deformation-induced transformation limit generates localized martensitic transformation domains.
The localized twin or martensitic domains absorb energy.
The localized twin or martensitic domains delay plastic flow.
The twin- or transformation-mediated response enhances strength.
The twin- or transformation-mediated response enhances ductility.
As-received CrMnFeCoNi has inherent chemical complexity and metastability.
As-received CrMnFeCoNi has the potential for deformation-induced twinning or transformation.
The proposed pre-strain treatment selectively suppresses twin formation without significantly altering other microstructural features.
Rapid formation of transient twin or martensitic domains absorbs strain energy during dynamic deformation.
Rapid formation of transient twin or martensitic domains delays dislocation motion.
Delayed dislocation motion caused by twin or martensitic domains increases work hardening.
Suppressing the relevant domains through pre-straining causes reduced dynamic strain hardening.
Suppressing the relevant domains through pre-straining causes earlier plastic flow.
Relative to the pre-strained baseline, the as-received alloy will show stronger in situ diffraction signatures of twin or transformation-domain formation.
Relative to the pre-strained baseline, the as-received alloy will exhibit greater work hardening.
Relative to the pre-strained baseline, the as-received alloy will exhibit a delayed onset of plastic flow.
The proposed mechanism should operate from cryogenic to room temperature, particularly at moderate stresses where the transformation driving force is marginal.
